audit: 2026-09-16 scheduled remote agent (fourth fire of the day): one 50 question batch across all four modules, published as eight files data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-16_d_<module>_1..2.json, two per module, split only so that each publishing call could carry complete literal content. Split 13 Paediatrics, 13 Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 12 Psychiatry and 12 Medicine; tier mix 26 L3, 20 L4 and 4 L5 with no L1 and no L2, taking the bank to 6642 with Paediatrics and Obstetrics on 1661 and Psychiatry and Medicine on 1660. Cell selection: the live matrix before this fire showed all four modules exactly level on 1648, with L3 deficits against the ideal 50 per cent of 13.66 points in Paediatrics, 13.22 in Obstetrics, 12.44 in Medicine and 11.53 in Psychiatry, L4 deficits against 45 per cent of 13.08, 12.59, 11.69 and 10.52 respectively, and L5 at 5.04 per cent in every module, a deficit of about minus 0.04 points. The strict per question argmax remains degenerate for the eleventh consecutive fire: run without the tie break it placed 44 of 50 questions into Paediatrics alone, because a single addition moves a module proportion by only about 0.04 points while leaving the other three modules untouched, so the same cell wins for a dozen iterations. Applying the routine's tie break clause, which treats cells within 0.5 percentage points as tied and resolves toward the lower module total, spread the batch across Paediatrics and Obstetrics but still produced zero Psychiatry and zero Medicine questions. This fire therefore allocated 13/13/12/12, giving the extra pair to the two modules carrying the largest L3 deficits, and within each module followed the ideal tier shape weighted toward L3 because its deficit leads L4 by 0.6 to 1.0 points everywhere. L5 was held at one per module rather than allowed to decay, since a strict reading generates no L5 at all. The structural point for the maintainer stands and is now well evidenced: because L5 sits at target its deficit can never approach the 11 to 14 point deficits carried by L3 and L4, and because the legacy L2 block of 353 to 422 questions per module sits permanently in the denominator, those L3 and L4 deficits can never close either, so the argmax will never select an L5 cell. The tier needs an explicit per batch quota if sustained L5 growth is wanted. Audit: valid JSON on all eight files, zero em-dashes and zero non-ASCII characters, zero banned tokens, every question difficulty 3, 4 or 5, answer-length parity max to min at or under 1.35 on all 50, correct letters exactly 10 per letter A to E after a programmatic rotation pass that preserved option content, source_refs all resolving to declared source labels, at least two sources per question with an Australian source first, reference_ranges keys all valid, vitals in fixed order or compressed to within normal limits, data_table values all flat strings, no lead-in guideline leak, no parenthetical qualifier in any correct option, no weight-based dose arithmetic in any lead-in, candidate positioned as the treating doctor throughout, explanation.summary 3 to 5 sentences with 5 key points and a specific pearl on every question. Three defects were found on audit and fixed before publication: three stray quotation marks inside source attributions that broke JSON in two files; a correct option uniquely carrying a numeral in the toddler iron deficiency item, corrected by writing a distractor's review interval in digits; and an inappropriate gcs reference_ranges key on the bulimia nervosa item. scripts/dupe_gate.py --new passed on the first run against the 6592 pre-existing questions with zero duplicates and, unlike the previous fire, zero pairs in the 0.62 to 0.69 review band; intra-batch self comparison also returned zero pairs at any band. No threshold was altered and the script was not modified. Pre-writing screening was heavier this fire than last: 77 candidate decision points were scored against the bank using the gate's own similarity metric before any question was written, and 27 were discarded at that stage for scoring 0.55 or above, among them clozapine myocarditis, refugee post traumatic stress disorder, synpharyngitic haematuria, allopurinol drug reaction with eosinophilia, adrenal crisis on prednisolone, insomnia in an older adult, osteoporosis treatment selection, postmenopausal bleeding with a 6 mm endometrium, complex adnexal mass triage, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, biliary atresia, tinea capitis, infantile haemangioma, coeliac serology on a gluten free diet, absent red reflex, tricyclic overdose, Lewy body hallucinations, premenstrual dysphoric disorder, prolonged grief, anorexia admission criteria and molar pregnancy surveillance.
